Why the WordPress and Drupal counts differ

WordPress stores pages, posts, attachments, menus, revisions, field definitions and plugin logs in one wp_posts table. Drupal lists authored pages under Content and stores files, menus and page components separately. Comparing those totals directly overstates the content gap.

        Coverage and source notes

        What this report includes

        Every row of the source wp_posts table is listed once in the main inventory, including unpublished pages and historical records. The media tab is a second view of the same attachment rows.

        Excerpts are plain-text previews, limited to 700 characters. Full preserved editorial content remains in Drupal or the local preservation dataset. A blank post body may be populated by theme templates or custom fields on the original site.

        Source dates are WordPress database timestamps, reproduced without assuming a timezone. The report generation time is shown in India Standard Time.

        Private and historical material

        This file is stored outside Drupal’s public web/ directory. It can include private titles, drafts and revision excerpts and is intended for local review.

          WordPress private/draft status is shown separately from Drupal publication status. Historical feed/test content is not evidence of a missing public page.

          Verification boundaries

          The original 344 migrated nodes were checked against their source fixture, including aliases, bodies, custom fields, component values and source hashes. New coverage is drawn from the additive import’s completion report.

          “Inventory only” identifies operational logs or WordPress implementation configuration. These are accounted for without recreating obsolete WordPress plugin behavior in Drupal. “Pending” or “Missing file” means the report has no completed destination evidence.

          Primary navigation and embedded privacy/quote content can have Drupal menu or component destinations instead of standalone nodes.

          Content written in theme templates

          Source taxonomy terms
